info.bio: Mudhoney es una de las bandas pioneras del movimiento grunge. Formada en la ciudad de Seattle tras la disolución de Green River, grupo en el que estaban Stone Gossard y Jeff Ament (luego en Pearl Jam) y Steve Turner y Mark Arm quienes luego formarían Mudhoney junto al baterista Dan Peters y al bajista Matt Lukin. En 1987 sacan su EP debut, Superfuzz Bigmuff, el cual contiene su canción más famosa: Touch Me I'm Sick. Su música se caracteriza por un punk energético con algo de psicodelia y mucho garage.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Ahead of Their Time in 1988
podcast.body: In 1988, the broader music world was not yet ready for Mudhoney's sound and attitude, as rock music was still dominated by hair metal and alternative rock remained largely marginalized. Additionally, Seattle was considered off the beaten track, hindering recognition. "More importantly, music at large wasn't really ready for this sound and attitude. Things were still all about hair metal in 1988. Rock music was still dominant, and any kind of alt rock was still very much in the margins. Besides, Seattle was way off the beaten track in those days, and no one paid attention to what was happening there."

podcast.title: Anticipating the Grunge Explosion
podcast.body: Despite their early presence, Mudhoney saw the grunge sound they pioneered explode into global prominence within two and a half years, largely thanks to bands like Soundgarden, Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Alice in Chains, underscoring that they had accurately predicted the future of rock but were too early for widespread acceptance. "Imagine how Mudhoney must have felt to see a sound they'd play in here blow up without them."

podcast.title: Associated with Grunge Movement (Mid-90s)
podcast.body: Mudhoney was grouped with other bands like Stone Temple Pilots and Soundgarden under the Grunge umbrella, dominant in North America in the early and mid-90s. "We also had the Stone Temple pilots in screaming trees, Allison Chains, Mud Honey, Tad, and a ton of others who were all placed under the same Grunge umbrella."

podcast.title: Band Name Origin - Russ Meyer Film
podcast.body: The band's name was derived from a softcore porn film directed by Russ Meyer, reflecting an edgy and unconventional aesthetic aligned with their music. "And their name came from a softcore porn film directed by Russ Meyer."

podcast.title: Early Seattle Grunge Pioneers
podcast.body: Mudhoney emerged on the Seattle scene in 1988, delivering a "dark, sludgy, tuned-down guitar sound" before almost any other band in the region had adopted such a style, positioning them at the vanguard of the burgeoning grunge movement. "They arrived on the Seattle scene in 1988 with a dark, sludgy, tuned-down guitar sound before almost anyone else in the region was into that sort of thing."

podcast.title: Early Subpop Roster
podcast.body: Mudhoney was one of the local groups that was part of Subpop's roster in the middle of 1988, when the label was establishing itself as a respected independent entity. "The roster featured local groups like Soundgarden, Screaming Trees and Mud Honey."

podcast.title: Mark Arm in Ron Ashton's Band
podcast.body: Mark Arm of Mudhoney was a member of a band that Ron Ashton played in after The Stooges' initial breakup. "Ron Ashton played in a series of bands, none of which did much, although there was the group that featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, also Mark Arm of Mudhoney and Jay Mascus of Dinosaur Jr."

podcast.title: Sub Pop Partnership and Limited Promotion
podcast.body: Mudhoney came to the attention of Bruce Pavitt, a partner in the "tiny struggling local record label" Sub Pop, who liked them enough to release their first single. However, Sub Pop's perpetual financial difficulties meant it lacked the resources to promote their releases widely, limiting their global reach. "They eventually came to the attention of Bruce Pavitt, one of the partners in a tiny struggling local record label called Subpop. He liked them enough to release a single."

xref.body: Green River ceased to exist in 1987, and from its survivors, including Mark Arm and Steve Turner, the band Mudhoney was formed, continuing the trajectory of early grunge music. "When they died in 1987, some survivors, including Mark and Steve, formed Mudhoney."

xref.title: Pioneering Recording at Reciprocal Recording
xref.body: Bam Bam made their first record, the "Villains" EP, in 1984 at Reciprocal Recording. This made them the first Grunge band to record at that studio, which later became famous for hosting bands like Nirvana, Alice in Chains, Soundgarden, The Melvins, and Mudhoney. "They used reciprocal recording, making them the first Grunge band to make music there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ron Ashton's Estrangement and Side Projects
xref.body: After the initial breakup of The Stooges, Ron Ashton was estranged from the group due to the "death trip" drug use. He later played in several bands that didn't achieve significant success, though one group featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, Mark Arm of Mudhoney, and J Mascis of Dinosaur Jr. He also pursued acting, appearing in the original *Texas Chainsaw Massacre* (1974). "Ron Ashton played in a series of bands, none of which did much, although there was the group that featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, also Mark Arm of Mudhoney and Jay Mascus of Dinosaur Jr."
